records.source_statement: Chapter XLIX 'Of Marriage' begins below the divider after the preceding forty-three general horary aphorisms.
limitations: This heading belongs to Chapter XLIX, not the previous section.

records.source_statement: First house/lord, Moon and Moon's separating planet signify the querent.
limitations: Separate the Moon's past separation from her later application.

records.source_statement: Seventh house/lord and planet to which Moon applies signify the desired partner.
For a male querent, Lilly adds Sun and Moon to his natural significators.
limitations: Historical gendered convention, not modern relationship evidence.

records.source_statement: For a female querent, Lilly adds Venus and Moon as natural significators.
Ascendant lord or Moon applying to seventh lord predicts desire fulfilled with much petitioning and solicitation.
limitations: Direction first-to-seventh and labour condition essential.

records.source_statement: Square or opposition with reception may accomplish marriage slowly with labour and trouble.
limitations: Both hard aspect and reception required, not a generic positive.

records.source_statement: Seventh lord applying to first lord, or Moon's applying planet to the separating planet, or seventh lord in ascendant, suggests easier marriage with sought partner's goodwill.
limitations: Trine or sextile especially favoured; preserve directed role.

records.source_statement: A separately headed set of aphorisms is attributed to Alkindus concerning marriage.
limitations: Lilly-mediated attribution, underlying Al-Kindi source uncollated.

records.source_statement: Alkindus passage presents ascendant lord applying to seventh lord by trine or sextile as a favourable marriage sign.
limitations: Printed marginal note adds reverse seventh-to-first possibility.

records.source_statement: Moon applying to Venus, Moon strong in motion and both having essential dignity, is another source completion configuration.
limitations: Do not omit strength and dignity.

records.source_statement: Venus beholding Sun while Sun has ascendant dignity or aspect to ascendant lord supplies another favourable channel.
limitations: Compound conditions, not any Sun/Venus aspect.

records.source_statement: Cadent significators not regarding each other, particularly without lords' regard, can begin with hopes but end after delays without marriage.
limitations: Early hopeful signal is not the actual outcome.

records.source_statement: Angular relevant significators with mutual aspects may ultimately produce marriage despite initial despair even by square/opposition.
limitations: Source says consent and providence are required, no observed outcome.

records.source_statement: Heading 'Of Marriage, whether it shall take effect or no?' opens another section and role assignments before page338.
limitations: This is not a second printed chapter.

records.source_statement: New section repeats first lord/Moon/Moon's separating planet for querent and seventh lord/Moon's applying planet for the desired partner.
limitations: Includes sex-specific Sun or Venus supplements across page boundary.
